look_here_first: Start with leaf architecture, not just leaflet count. Texas barberry usually has 5–9 leaflets, often with a reduced basal pair close to the rachis base, a dull gray-green reticulate surface, and a more open taller shrub form than agarita.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: basal leaflet pair often strongly reduced

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: more open less rounded shrub habit

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: yellow spring flowers and variable pale-to-reddish fruits

lookalikes.differences: Agarita is typically trifoliolate and denser. Hybrids commonly have 5–7 leaflets but lack the distinctive reduced basal leaflet pair of true B. swaseyi; use leaflet structure, bracts, and surface texture together.
